questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: After 'Little' at the start of a sentence, use inversion with 'did': Little did he know.

wrongReasons.little he knew that his life was about t: After 'Little' at the start of a sentence, we need inversion with an auxiliary: Little did he know.

questions.wrong: Little he knew that his life was about to change.
solutions: Little did he know that his life was about to change.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: Inverted second conditional: 'Were I you' (no 'to be' after 'Were I').

wrongReasons.were i to be you, i would accept the off: 'Were I to' is used with other verbs (Were I to leave...). With 'be' we say 'Were I you' or 'If I were you'.

questions.wrong: Were I to be you, I would accept the offer.
solutions: Were I you, I would accept the offer.
If I were you, I would accept the offer.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: A demand after 'insist that' uses the subjunctive (base form) or 'should' + base form: She insisted that he be told.

wrongReasons.the lawyer insisted that his client is r: This is a demand, not a fact, so formal English uses 'be' after 'insisted that'.
wrongReasons.the lawyer insisted that his client was: 'was released' reports a fact; a demand needs 'be released' or 'should be released'.

questions.wrong: The lawyer insisted that his client is released at once.
solutions: The lawyer insisted that his client be released at once.
The lawyer insisted that his client should be released at once.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: After 'Only when' + clause at the start, the main clause needs inversion: Only when he left did I relax.

wrongReasons.only when the lights went out we noticed: After 'Only when …' the main clause must be inverted: did we notice.
wrongReasons.only when the lights went out did we not: After 'did', use the base form 'notice', not 'noticed'.

questions.wrong: Only when the lights went out we noticed the smell of smoke.
solutions: Only when the lights went out did we notice the smell of smoke.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: In an 'It was … that' cleft, when the focus is a phrase like 'in 2010', use 'that': It was in Rome that they met.

wrongReasons.it was in 2010 when the company was foun: When the focus is a phrase with 'in', the cleft needs 'that', not 'when'.

questions.wrong: It was in 2010 when the company was founded.
solutions: It was in 2010 that the company was founded.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: In the third conditional, the if-clause uses the past perfect, not 'would have': If she had called, I would have answered.

wrongReasons.if i would have known, i would have help: 'would have' is not used in the if-clause; use the past perfect: If I had known.
wrongReasons.if i knew, i would have helped you: 'knew' refers to the present; for the past use 'had known'.

questions.wrong: If I would have known, I would have helped you.
solutions: If I had known, I would have helped you.
Had I known, I would have helped you.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: For a past action after 'is said', use the perfect infinitive: He is said to have left.

wrongReasons.she is said to be won the award twice: 'to be won' is passive and makes no sense here; use 'to have won'.
wrongReasons.she is said to has won the award twice: After 'to' use the base form 'have', not 'has'.

questions.wrong: She is said to be won the award twice.
solutions: She is said to have won the award twice.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: 'Elicit' is a verb meaning to draw out a reaction or information; 'illicit' is an adjective meaning illegal.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: After 'So' + adjective at the start, the verb comes before the subject: So strong was the wind that trees fell.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: For a present situation we would like to be different, use 'wish' + past simple ('were' for all persons): I wish it were summer.
